title: Certificate of Analysis Extraction and Spec Matching
summary: Read supplier and in-house certificates of analysis, extract every test result and compare it with your approved specification, so QC sees out-of-limit, missing and mismatched lines at a glance.

seo.title: COA Extraction and Specification Matching | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that extracts results from supplier COAs, matches them to approved specifications and flags out-of-limit, missing and mismatched lines for QC.

problem.intro: Every lot of API, excipient and packaging material arrives with a supplier certificate of analysis, each in its own layout. QC compares the COA line by line with the approved specification and vendor approval before sampling and testing, and similar checks repeat for finished-product COAs sent to customers.

pain_points.title: Formats vary by supplier
pain_points.detail: Test names, units and limit expressions differ between suppliers, so a COA cannot be checked with a fixed template.

pain_points.title: Specification drift
pain_points.detail: Suppliers sometimes quote an older pharmacopoeia edition or their own limits, which is easy to miss when the result itself passes.

pain_points.title: Missing tests
pain_points.detail: A residual solvent, microbial or elemental impurity test that is in your specification but absent from the COA can slip through a quick visual check.

pain_points.title: Lot and date mismatches
pain_points.detail: Batch numbers and manufacture or retest dates on the COA do not always match the container label, invoice or goods receipt note.

solution.overview: We build a COA checking pipeline that reads each certificate, whether a digital PDF or a scan, and extracts material, supplier, batch, dates and every test with its result, unit and limit. Test names are mapped to your specification through a maintained synonym list, units are normalised, and each result is compared with your approved limit. The system also checks that every specified test is present, that the cited pharmacopoeia matches your specification, and that batch and dates match the goods receipt. QC sees a pass, flag or missing status for every line, with the source shown beside it.
capabilities: Extracts tests, results, units and limits from digital and scanned COAs in any supplier layout
Maps supplier test names to your specification through a QC-approved synonym library
Normalises units and limit expressions such as NMT, NLT and ranges
Flags out-of-limit results, missing tests and differing pharmacopoeia references
Matches batch number and dates against the goods receipt note and label
Keeps a per-supplier history to show results drifting towards limits

workflow.title: Receive the COA
workflow.detail: COAs arrive with the consignment, by email or from a supplier portal, and are linked to the goods receipt note.

workflow.title: Extract test data
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM extract header details and the test table with results, units and limits.

workflow.title: Map to specification
workflow.detail: Each test is mapped to the approved specification for that material and vendor, and units are normalised.

workflow.title: Compare and check completeness
workflow.detail: Results are compared with limits, missing tests are listed, and batch and dates are matched to the goods receipt.

workflow.title: QC review
workflow.detail: Flags, unmapped tests and low-confidence values go to a QC reviewer, who accepts, rejects or raises a query with the supplier.

workflow.title: Record the outcome
workflow.detail: Checked COA data is stored against the lot in LIMS or ERP with the reviewer's decision.

inputs: Supplier COAs for APIs, excipients and packaging materials
Approved material specifications and approved vendor list
Goods receipt notes and supplier invoices
Pharmacopoeia references cited in your specifications
outputs: Line-by-line comparison with pass, flag or missing status
List of out-of-limit results and absent tests
Batch and date mismatch alerts against the goods receipt
Structured COA data stored against the lot
Supplier-wise trend of results near limits
human_in_the_loop: QC reviews every flagged line, unmapped test and low-confidence value, and decides whether to accept the COA, query the supplier or reject the lot. The COA check supports, and does not replace, your sampling and testing programme and the QA release decision.
integrations: LIMS such as LabWare, LabVantage or STARLIMS
ERP such as SAP for goods receipt and lot status
Document management system for approved specifications
QMS for supplier complaints and CAPA
guardrails: New test-name synonyms added only after QC approval
Specifications pulled from the effective version only
No automatic lot release; status changes stay with QC and QA
Low-confidence values always shown next to the source image
Periodic re-check of a sample of cleared COAs by QC
compliance_notes: Supports vendor qualification and material control expectations under GMP, including India's revised Schedule M.
Where COA data feeds GMP decisions, records and audit trails are designed to align with 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.

pilot.scope: A group of high-volume raw materials from a few suppliers, using recent COAs already reviewed by QC, followed by a short live run.
deliverables: Synonym and unit library for the pilot materials
Accuracy report against QC's own COA reviews
Plan to extend to the remaining materials

what_we_measure.how: Extracted results and limits compared with QC-verified values for the same COAs.
Supplier test names checked by QC for correct mapping to the specification.
QC decision recorded against each flag raised.
Timed checks on comparable COAs with and without the pipeline.

faqs.q: Does this replace our COA review SOP?
faqs.a: No. The pipeline does the reading and comparing, and your SOP is updated to describe how QC reviews its output. Lot release decisions stay with QC and QA.

faqs.q: What about COAs that are not in English?
faqs.a: Most supplier COAs are in English or bilingual. Where a supplier issues COAs only in another language, we test extraction on samples during the pilot and report results per supplier.

faqs.q: Can it check pharmacopoeia limits directly?
faqs.a: It checks against your approved specification, which already reflects the monograph you follow. It also flags when a supplier cites a different pharmacopoeia or edition, so QC can decide whether that matters.

faqs.q: Will it work for the finished-product COAs we issue?
faqs.a: Yes. The same comparison can check COAs generated from LIMS before they go to customers or regulators, catching transcription errors and missing tests.
